output.brief: The Android drop is not caused by release 6.14, the Android OS patch, or credential stuffing. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC, Corvane auto-updated its edge rules. A new rule, AUTO-LIB-17, blocks any password-login request from the app's networking library that has no edge session cookie. It returns HTTP 403. About 9,600 requests a day are blocked, from 41,300 install IDs, and 92% of those had logged in successfully before. So these are real customers, not bots. The failures started within one minute on every app version, OS version and patch state. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are untouched. Password success fell from 96% to 8%. Version 6.14 is only 5% of attempts and fails at the same rate as older versions, so a rollback would not help. Raising bot sensitivity or excluding blocked attempts from the KPI would make things worse and hide the problem. Next step: have Corvane set the new rule to log-only on the mobile password path (A1), keeping the other protections on. Then confirm in telemetry that password success returns to about 96%. Also ask Corvane for a proper fix and for advance notice of rule changes. Confidence is high. The call-volume link to the drop is only loosely supported, because the fee mailing also raised calls.
